newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity prices ease in quiet July expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity prices ease in quiet July expiry.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended lower Wednesday in a quiet July expiry that showed some weakness on generation unit returns and bearish weather in the Pacific Northwest, industry sources said.

July Palo Verde (PV) ended down 33 cents at $33.02 following exchanges in a range of $32.50-33.75 per megawatt hour (MWh), while August PV closed down 52 cents at $34.33 after trades in a range of $34.00-34.90 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) settled down 46 cents at $20.40 after exchanges in a range of $20.00-20.95, while August finished down 80 cents at $23.10 following trades at $23.00-23.90 per MWh.
August was expected to show continued gradual declines as power generation units returned to service from spring maintenance and refueling programs, sources said.
"We had a lot of generation go off line earlier this spring and (futures prices) climbed strongly, but the decline is always much more gradual," said one Western futures broker.
The July contract, on its first day of trade as the front month in late May, settled with COB at $22.69 and PV at $30.31 per MWh.
July COB and PV began Wednesday stronger on news the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant near Phoenix, Ariz., had cut power to 60 percent overnight to repair re-heater tubes.
However, the futures backed off later following news the plant was in the process of ramping back up to full power.
July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended down 5.9 cents at $2.227 per million British thermal units in technical selling following six consecutive up days.
Meteorologists called for temperatures in the Northwest to run below early summer norms through next week, while those in the Southwest would average mostly near to above normal.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 609 COB and 808 PV contracts had traded.
